headline: Every journey starts with a question.
sub: The boat is a potential client. The bay is a business.
pov: Low, close tracking shot beside one blue boat. Businesses sit on the distant horizon.
action: A prospective buyer asks ChatGPT: “Which payment provider is the best?” A readable conversation opens above the boat.
takeaway: People use AI and search to decide which businesses to consider. The grey logo tells us where this buyer is looking.
motion: 0–6%: follow the boat for several hull lengths. 6–13%: ease to a stop; hold the question and a clarifying answer. The boat stays visible beneath the conversation. No automatic typing race.
decision: Does the visitor immediately understand that the boat is a person looking for a business?

headline: Being an option comes before being chosen.
sub: Stay with the buyer as they cross open water toward a business they discovered.
pov: Crane up into a wide map, then travel with the same boat toward a genuinely distant competitor bay.
action: An illustrative answer names Provider A and Provider B. Your business is absent in this sample. The buyer follows one option across a long stretch of water.
takeaway: If your business is missing from relevant answers, potential clients may consider competitors first. A visit is consideration, not a purchase.
motion: 13–20%: hold the answer. 20–31%: track a continuous curved voyage. Competitor is 4–6 main-bay widths away in the future world. Start small on the horizon; approach through camera travel. Never shrink the boat to reset it.
decision: Can you follow the same buyer from the question to the competitor, and feel the distance?

headline: SailTru makes the missing route visible.
sub: Track search and AI visibility. Compare competitors. Find what is worth improving.
pov: Pull back from the destination into the market; then bring a stable evidence card forward.
action: The buyer’s question becomes a tracked query across Google, ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity. A competitor comparison identifies a specific unanswered buyer question.
takeaway: SailTru tracks SEO and GEO, compares businesses, investigates gaps and prioritizes actions. Provider icons are channels, never worker boats.
motion: 31–38%: widen the view to reconnect the two bays. 38–47%: reveal one finding on a fixed card. Routes recede while the evidence is read. No rotating logos or radar sweep behind text.
decision: Is the recommendation supported by a concrete observation rather than a vague visibility score?

headline: Build a business that is easier to discover and choose.
sub: The same bay improves as SailTru helps implement the work.
pov: Descend into your bay. Keep the shoreline identity, beach and buildings continuous.
action: A useful fees-and-integrations page replaces a vague page. Clearer information makes the business easier to evaluate; the pier represents the next step. New berths appear as the visitor experience improves.
takeaway: SailTru helps carry out the changes: useful content, technical clarity and a better path from discovery to enquiry. The growing bay is a visual metaphor, not a promised result.
motion: 47–53%: arrive at the same bay from its seaward approach. 53–63%: show the page improvement first, then extend the pier from 4 to 8 berths. One change at a time; hold the completed state.
decision: Can you name the actual business improvement behind the harbour transformation?

headline: A clearer route from discovery to your business.
sub: Return to the buyer’s point of view and close the loop.
pov: Return to a close boat-following shot, then rise gently to reveal your bay filling the destination view.
action: In a later illustrative answer, your business is one option to compare. The same blue buyer boat takes a long approach, reads your page and visits a berth. Other buyers continue toward other businesses.
takeaway: The aim is to be discoverable and worth considering. SailTru checks whether changes improve actual visibility and enquiries; appearance and visits are not guaranteed.
motion: 63–69%: hold the refreshed answer with the same query. 69–82%: follow a continuous route through open water, coastline and harbour entrance. Maintain readable boat size with camera distance; slow only for docking.
decision: Is the return journey satisfying without suggesting that one edit guarantees a recommendation or a sale?

headline: More room for the people who find you.
sub: End with a large, living bay—and a team with more capacity to look after its visitors.
pov: Settle into a wide elevated view: your bay dominates the composition, with the competitor distant on the horizon.
action: The pier grows to 12 berths. Boats with grey Google, ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity symbols arrive and depart. Inside the business, optional bespoke AI workflows organize work and free the team’s desk.
takeaway: SailTru combines ongoing visibility improvement with optional bespoke AI solutions and agent teams. All boats remain potential clients; AI works inside the business.
motion: 82–90%: settle into the completed bay; reveal 8 → 12 berths. 90–100%: hold the composition. Ambient arrivals and departures loop on separate lanes. The optional office inset handles research, follow-up drafts and reporting with human review.
decision: Does the final scene show a living business, clear service choices and more team capacity without treating boats as AI agents?
